---
title: "Cache and mirror backend"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment  = "#>"
)
```

`cvmdata` ships two interchangeable backends behind `cvm_fetch()` and a
multi-layer disk cache that both backends share. This article walks
through the contract, the pipeline that keeps the mirror fresh, and
the workflows for switching between backends, inspecting the cache,
and tuning the TTL and eviction options.

```{r setup}
library(cvmdata)
```

## Reference: backends and caches

### Source backends

| Backend    | What it queries                                  | When to prefer it                                                                 |
|------------|--------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `"mirror"` | Parquet snapshots in GitHub Releases named `mirror-<group>-<dataset>-latest`, queried via DuckDB. | Default from v0.1.0. ~30× faster on yearly bundles; staleness bounded by the weekly refresh window vs. CVM live. |
| `"cvm"`    | The CVM Open Data Portal over HTTP (`dados.cvm.gov.br`). | Highest freshness — bytes are direct from the regulator. Opt in when you need the latest publication within the refresh window. |

The active backend is selected at three precedence levels: an
explicit `source = ...` argument to `cvm_fetch()` wins over the option
`cvmdata.source` (set via `cvm_source_set()`), which in turn wins over
the built-in default returned by `cvm_source_get()`.

The mirror is maintained by the package author, not by the CVM. Its
content is the CVM's, re-encoded to UTF-8, typed according to the CVM
data dictionary and partitioned by year; no value is altered. Two
consequences are worth knowing before you rely on the default. First,
the mirror can lag the portal by up to the weekly refresh window.
Second, the ETL skips a year whose CSV the CVM publishes with no data
rows, so the mirror's inventory for a table may end earlier than the
portal's list of years (the `cvm` backend returns such a year as zero
rows instead). Every skip is recorded, with its reason, in the
`__source_hash.json` sidecar of the release, and the error you get when
asking the mirror for a missing year quotes it: whether the CVM
published the CSV with the header only, or did not include it in the
yearly ZIP at all.

### Data licence and attribution

The CVM publishes every dataset covered by the package under the
[Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL)
v1.0](https://opendatacommons.org/licenses/odbl/1-0/), declared on
each dataset page of the portal. The mirror is a *derivative database*
in the terms of that licence and is redistributed under the ODbL as
well; the release notes of every `mirror-*-latest` release carry the
notice. When you redistribute data obtained through `cvmdata`, or a
database derived from it, keep the attribution:

> Contains data from the Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM) Open
> Data Portal, <https://dados.cvm.gov.br/>, made available under the
> Open Data Commons Open Database License (ODbL) v1.0.

The full notice, with what the licence asks of you, is in the
repository's
[`DATA-LICENSE.md`](https://github.com/SidneyBissoli/cvmdata/blob/main/DATA-LICENSE.md).
The package code is MIT licensed; the data is not.

### Cache layers

| Layer | Location                                                         | Content                                          | Invalidation        |
|-------|------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------|---------------------|
| L1    | `<cache>/raw/<group>/<dataset>/[<year>/]`                        | Raw CVM CSV (CAD) or yearly ZIPs (DFP/ITR/FRE) + extracted CSVs, with `*.etag.rds` sidecars. | HTTP HEAD with ETag / Last-Modified, throttled by `options(cvmdata.cache_ttl_seconds)` (default 30 days). |
| L3    | `<cache>/parquet/<group>/<dataset>/<table>/[report_type=R/]year=Y/part-0.parquet` | Parquet downloaded from the mirror.            | Content-addressed via the `<cache>/parquet/<group>/<dataset>/__source_hash.json` sidecar — the whole dataset tree is evicted when the upstream hash changes. |
| L4    | In-session memory.                                               | Planned for v0.2.                                | —                   |

The `<group>` segment is the CKAN group slug returned by
`cvm_groups()` (e.g. `"companhias"` for the four datasets shipped in
v0.1.0). Caches written by `cvmdata` ≤ 0.0.x without the segment are
migrated automatically the first time a 0.1.x session touches them.

`cvm_cache_path()` returns the cache root; `cvm_cache_set_path()`
relocates it; `cvm_cache_info()` lists every artifact with its size,
ETag and timestamps; `cvm_cache_clear()` evicts (with `what` of
`"all"`, `"raw"`, or `"parquet"`).

```{r cache-root}
cvm_cache_path()
cvm_source_get()
```

## Mirror pipeline validation

Every weekly mirror publish runs a hybrid validation step
(`inst/etl/02b-validate.R`) between parquet generation and upload. The
checks are split into two tiers: *hard* failures block the publish
(the matrix job exits 1 and the previous mirror release stays in
place), *soft* failures emit a warning and let the publish proceed.
The validation markdown report is uploaded as a workflow artifact so
post-hoc inspection is always available, regardless of outcome.

| Check                                       | Severity | Applies to                                              |
|---------------------------------------------|----------|---------------------------------------------------------|
| Parquet file exists                         | hard     | Every (table, year, report_type) implied by the schema |
| Parquet readable by `arrow`                 | hard     | Every produced parquet                                  |
| `n_rows > 0`                                | hard     | Every produced parquet                                  |
| Identifier column (`cnpj_cia` / `cnpj_companhia`) is character | hard | Tables that carry one                                  |
| `vl_conta` is numeric                       | hard     | Tables that declare `multiply_by_scale`                |
| Identifier values match the CVM CNPJ regex  | soft     | Tables with `cnpj_cia` / `cnpj_companhia`              |
| `cd_cvm` values are all-digits              | soft     | Tables with `cd_cvm`                                    |
| `dt_refer` / `data_referencia` within `[first_year, today + 1y]` | soft | Tables with a publish-date column                      |

The hybrid scope follows the decisions of session 3.14: universal
invariants live in code (no per-dataset YAMLs), hard checks bound the
worst case (empty / unreadable / wrong-type), soft checks bound the
content noise the CVM occasionally publishes. New checks land in the
same script; documenting them here is the rOpenSci-auditable surface.

### Superseded filings

Each CVM annual file carries only the filing delivered last for every
company and reference date, so a restatement silently replaces the
previous numbers in the file, and the mirror followed suit until
2026-10. Since then the publish step compares, for every partition
whose content hash moved, the parquet of the previous release with the
new one, filing by filing, and appends the rows of the filings that
were replaced or dropped to a cumulative history asset of the same
partition, named `<table>__report_type=R__year=Y__history.parquet`,
with two extra columns: `superseded_at` (the ETL run, UTC) and
`superseded_by_versao` (the `versao` of the replacing filing, `NA` when
the filing vanished). A filing counts as changed by the content of its
rows, not by a new `versao` or document id with the same numbers (the
`submissao` table already records every delivery). The `-latest`
parquets and `cvm_fetch()` are untouched: the client ignores the
history assets. Reading them through the package, and recovering
filings superseded before the history existed, are planned separately
(see the roadmap).

## Workflow 1 — Working with the mirror (default)

From v0.1.0 the mirror is the default backend, so `cvm_fetch()`
routes every call through DuckDB without further configuration. The
snippet below makes the choice explicit (helpful in scripts that may
inherit a different session option) and exercises both the cold and
warm cache paths:

```{r workflow-1-show, eval = FALSE}
# Make the choice explicit (a no-op when the option is already unset
# from the built-in default).
cvm_source_set("mirror")

# First call: the mirror's release inventory is fetched once via the
# GitHub REST API, parquet assets are downloaded into the L3 cache, and
# DuckDB reads them from disk.
bb_bpa_mirror <- cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  year = 2024,
  basis = "ind"
)

# Second call: the L3 cache short-circuits the download; the API
# inventory is reused from the session cache; only DuckDB runs.
cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  year = 2024,
  basis = "ind"
)
```

The argument `source = ...` to `cvm_fetch()` always overrides the
option, so a single call can fall back to the CVM portal without
disturbing the session-wide setting:

```{r workflow-1-override, eval = FALSE}
# Persisted setting is "mirror"; this one call still queries CVM live.
cvm_fetch(
  "dfp", "bpa",
  cnpj = "00.000.000/0001-91",
  year = 2024,
  basis = "ind",
  source = "cvm"
)
```

## Workflow 2 — CVM vs Mirror equivalence

The mirror backend returns tibbles that are column- and type-equivalent
to the CVM HTTP path on the common columns. The mirror additionally
attaches a `year` partition column reattached from the asset filename
— it is not present on the CVM path because the CVM CSV does not carry
it. The `report_type` partition the mirror also carries is exposed by
`cvm_fetch()` under the public name `basis`, on both backends, for the
tables that have the individual/consolidated split. The table below
was captured by
`data-raw/validate-mirror-end-to-end.R`, which runs the same four
calls through both backends and compares schemas:

```{r workflow-2-rds}
cmp <- readRDS(system.file(
  "extdata", "vignette-data", "cache-and-mirror",
  "cvm-vs-mirror.rds",
  package = "cvmdata"
))
knitr::kable(cmp)
```

Small `nrow` differences (e.g. ITR's `~0.2%`) are the expected staleness
window between the weekly cron and the live CVM portal — every
Tuesday at 04:00 BRT the mirror refreshes; chamadas during the rest
of the week may see CVM rows the mirror has not yet snapshotted. This
is feature, not bug: the mirror is a snapshot.

## Workflow 3 — Inspecting and clearing the cache

`cvm_cache_info()` walks the cache and returns one row per artifact:

```{r workflow-3-show, eval = FALSE}
info <- cvm_cache_info()
info

# Total bytes across all listed artifacts:
attr(info, "total_size_bytes")
```

The first column of `cvm_cache_info()` is `group`, mirroring the
on-disk layout — useful when later releases bring datasets from
multiple CKAN groups into the same cache.

`cvm_cache_clear()` accepts a `what` argument scoping the eviction to
L1 (`"raw"`), L3 (`"parquet"`), or both (`"all"`), plus an optional
`group` to restrict the eviction to a single CKAN group. The L3 mode
evicts by dataset because the partition layout nests year under
table:

```{r workflow-3-clear, eval = FALSE}
# Drop the mirror's local parquet copy for DFP only.
cvm_cache_clear(what = "parquet", dataset = "dfp", confirm = FALSE)

# Drop every artifact belonging to the "companhias" CKAN group
# (raw + parquet), leaving other groups intact.
cvm_cache_clear(what = "all", group = "companhias", confirm = FALSE)

# Reset everything (raw + parquet, all groups).
cvm_cache_clear(what = "all", confirm = FALSE)
```

In interactive sessions `confirm = TRUE` (the default) prompts via
`utils::askYesNo()`; batch scripts must pass `confirm = FALSE`.

## Workflow 4 — TTL and LRU eviction

Two options shape the cache's behaviour beyond explicit clears:

* `cvmdata.cache_ttl_seconds` (default `2592000`, i.e. 30 days)
  controls how often the L1 cache revalidates against CVM with an
  HTTP HEAD request. Set to `0` to revalidate on every call and to
  `Inf` to skip revalidation entirely until manual clear.
* `cvmdata.cache_max_size_mb` (default `100`) caps the size of L1.
  When total size exceeds 90% of the limit, the next download evicts
  the oldest units until the cache drops to 80% of the limit. Setting
  the option to `0`, a negative value, or `Inf` disables the eviction
  engine. The L3 mirror cache is content-addressed and not subject to
  size-based eviction.

```{r workflow-4-show, eval = FALSE}
# Force revalidation on every L1 hit.
options(cvmdata.cache_ttl_seconds = 0)

# Cap L1 at 250 MiB; LRU kicks in past 225 MiB and stops at 200 MiB.
options(cvmdata.cache_max_size_mb = 250)

# Subscribe to eviction notifications even in non-interactive runs.
options(cvmdata.cache_warn_evictions = TRUE)
```

Eviction emits the `cvmdata_warn_eviction` warning class
(interactive sessions get it for free; batch jobs honour the
`cache_warn_evictions` option). The aggregated message reports how
many units were removed and how much disk it freed.
